findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Correct the classification source: name the framework-set `evidence_sufficient: false` marker (`completion_reconcile._insufficiency_only` / top-level `result['evidence_sufficient']`) and the per-criterion `met=false`-with-marker vs `met=false`-without-marker (refutation) distinction as the signal, not `completion_failures.py` (which classifies runner-exception exhaustion, not per-criterion refutation).
evidence: Plan: 'Classification comes from the per-criterion verdict statuses the verifier already returns (completion_failures.py taxonomy); no new telemetry.'
src/rebar/llm/contracts.py:78-133 — VerdictFinding has {criterion, detail, severity, dimension, citations}; Criterion has {criterion, met:bool, citation, kind}; no REFUTED/INSUFFICIENT enum
src/rebar/llm/workflow/completion_failures.py:48-80 — _is_token_exhaustion classifies finish_reason=length/max_tokens/context_length_exceeded on runner exceptions, not per-criterion refutation
src/rebar/llm/completion_reconcile.py:117-126,198-208 — _insufficiency_only() + derived top-level result['evidence_sufficient']=False is the real 'insufficient AND no refutation' signal
findings.finding: The plan sources its refuted-vs-insufficient classification from a schema/module that does not carry that vocabulary: it names 'the per-criterion verdict statuses the verifier already returns (completion_failures.py taxonomy)', but the completion_verdict schema has no per-criterion status enum (findings carry only free-text detail+severity; criteria carry met:bool+citation+kind), and completion_failures.py classifies RUNNER-EXCEPTION exhaustion (finish_reason=length/max_tokens/context_length_exceeded), not per-criterion refutation. The actual signal is the framework-derived evidence_sufficient:false marker (completion_reconcile._insufficiency_only / result['evidence_sufficient']).
scenarios: Executor implements the classifier against completion_failures.py and finds no per-criterion refuted/insufficient statuses, then must reverse-engineer the true marker seam
The classifier keys on a non-existent status enum and never fires (or misfires)
findings.suggested_fix: Rewrite (2) to say: qualify for auto-resume iff the returned FAIL verdict carries top-level `evidence_sufficient == False` (equivalently `_insufficiency_only(result)` is true) — i.e. at least one unmet criterion carries the framework `evidence_sufficient: false` marker AND no unmet criterion is a genuine refutation (`met=false` WITHOUT the marker). Drop the `completion_failures.py`/'per-criterion verdict statuses' framing.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Specify which exhaustion surface the classifier inspects — the RETURNED FAIL verdict with `evidence_sufficient: false` vs the RAISED verdict-less `CompletionRecoveryError` — and state the fallback for the verdict-less raised case (resume, or fail fast without resume).
evidence: src/rebar/llm/workflow/gate_dispatch.py:718-723 — if res.status != 'succeeded' or verdict missing 'verdict' → raise_completion_workflow_failure (raises, returns no verdict)
src/rebar/llm/workflow/completion_recovery.py:201-211 — zero banked entries → raise CompletionRecoveryError (verdict-less, deliberate)
src/rebar/llm/completion_reconcile.py:202-208 — evidence_sufficient marker only exists on a RETURNED FAIL verdict, not on a raised exception
findings.finding: The plan's classification assumes a RETURNED FAIL verdict with per-criterion records, but exhaustion can also surface as a RAISED, verdict-less CompletionRecoveryError (produce_completion_verdict → raise_completion_workflow_failure when the run did not produce a verdict, e.g. zero banked verdicts or a recovery preflight fault). In that case no per-criterion verdict object reaches the seam to classify. The plan neither states which surface the classifier inspects nor specifies a fallback for the verdict-less raised case.
scenarios: First close exhausts with zero banked verdicts and raises CompletionRecoveryError; the classifier has no verdict to read evidence_sufficient from and either crashes or never resumes
Recovery preflight failure raises before any per-criterion record exists
findings.suggested_fix: Add to (2): classify on the returned FAIL verdict's `evidence_sufficient` marker; for a raised `CompletionRecoveryError` (verdict-less, e.g. zero-banked or preflight fault) state the intended behavior explicitly — either treat it as exhaustion-qualifying and resume, or fail fast to the operator — and cover it with a unit test alongside the existing (a)/(b)/(c) cases.

findings.checklist_item: - [ ] Confirm (in a comment or an AC assertion) that the verdict cache scope survives across resumption re-invocations within one close, so credited PASSes actually seed the re-run.
evidence: "The verdict cache seeds credited PASSes (existing behavior, no change needed); the fresh budget concentrates on remaining criteria ... concentration is emergent from cache hits consuming ~0 steps"
findings.finding: Resumption correctness DEPENDS on the verdict cache (Gerrit 1796) still holding the credited PASSes at re-invocation time; the plan asserts 'existing behavior, no change needed' but does not confirm consumers tolerate an empty/stale cache (e.g. cache eviction between invocations would silently defeat the concentration mechanism).
scenarios: Cache is scoped/evicted such that a re-invocation gets no cache hits — the resumption re-searches all criteria and exhausts again, making auto-resume a no-op that just burns budget.
